narrative.overview:
The page is a painting first. A slow WebGL sky of dark petrol smoke, warm plum and rust, three sigil rings cut into the paint around the logo, circuit traces running out to the edges, embers rising and a hatched, inked vignette in the corners. On it sits a single, centred stage: the DF27 logo, the season lettered in brass ink, one tracked line, and one beveled brass portal. Nothing else competes on the first screen.

Below the stage a veil darkens the painting to near-black and the page becomes a quiet single column: brass rubric headings between inked rules, a large ivory lead, what is announced, the last edition in figures, photographs in thin brass frames, the newsletter. The materials are few and old-world (ink, ivory, brass), and the one modern element, the cold aether light, is spent only on response: hover, focus, and the painting's own glow.
keyCharacteristics: An ink ground under a live painting; text lives on the veil, not on the paint.
Ivory type in one system sans; brass for ornament, labels and figures.
The aether light (cyan) means "this responds"; it never decorates at rest.
A beveled, eight-sided brass portal is the one button, once per screen.
Inked, slightly trembling strokes (the `aether-ink` filter) on every drawn line.
Centred and symmetric throughout; no cards, no grid of panels.

rules.name: The Cold Light Rule
rules.body: The aether colour is a response, never a resting colour: hover, focus, selected text, a field a failed submit points at, and the painting's glow only. A control at rest is ivory and brass; it turns aether when the visitor reaches it.

rules.name: The Three Materials Rule
rules.body: Ink, ivory and brass carry everything at rest. No new hue enters the page chrome; the painting's petrol, plum and rust stay inside the canvas and its CSS fallback gradients.

rules.name: The One Stack Rule
rules.body: The aether loads no web font. Bebas Neue, Special Elite and JetBrains Mono belong to the 2026 system (`docs/design-2026.md`) and never appear on a `TeaserLayout` page; nothing else is added either.

rules.name: The Label Voice Rule
rules.body: Small captions and headings speak in the label voice: uppercase, 600, tracked between 0.18em and 0.28em, always through `label()`. Running text is never uppercase.

rules.name: The Veil Rule
rules.body: Text never sits on the bright painting. Below the stage every band is on the veil; on the stage only the logo, the season, one label line (with a dark text shadow) and the portal sit over the paint, where the shader keeps the smoke darkest and calmest behind the logo.

rules.name: The Light Is Response Rule
rules.body: A glow is the aether light: only on the logo (part of the painting) and on the portal in response. Nothing else glows.

rules.name: The Brass Ornament Rule
rules.body: The inked rule ending in a diamond appears in exactly two places: either side of the season mark, and either side of a rubric heading (mirrored). It is never a divider, a bullet or a background.

rules.name: The One Portal Rule
rules.body: One solid portal per page, at most two portals per screen. The stage carries the solid one (the newsletter) and a framed one (the last edition's archive), side by side where both fit, stacked on a phone; the newsletter's submit is the only other, a full screen below.

dos: **Do** take every colour, size and space from the `:root.aether` tokens and the `_aether.scss` recipes.
**Do** set every caption and heading through `label()`, tracked 0.18–0.28em.
**Do** keep text below the stage on the veil.
**Do** give every animation and transition a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out; the painting becomes one still frame.
**Do** pass every drawn stroke through `aether-ink` so it reads as inked.
**Do** meet WCAG 2.2 AA; the `npm run a11y` axe sweep covers `/`.
donts: **Don't** use the aether colour at rest; it is hover, focus and the painting's glow.
**Don't** put a second solid portal on a page, more than two portals on a screen, or round a portal's corners.
**Don't** use the brass rule and diamond anywhere but the season mark and rubric headings.
**Don't** load a web font or bring a 2026 face (Bebas Neue, Special Elite, JetBrains Mono) onto a teaser page.
**Don't** add cards, box shadows or radius; depth is the painting and the veil.
**Don't** set text over the bright painting.
